title: Notes for Our Dog Sitter
text:
Dear Jenny,

Thank you for taking care of our dog, Waffles, while we are away. Here are some important notes.

Waffles eats breakfast at seven o'clock and dinner at five o'clock. Please give him one scoop of dog food and a few {plural noun} as a treat. He likes his bowl to be {adjective}.

Waffles needs to go for a walk two times a day. He will try to {verb} at every squirrel he sees. Hold the leash {adverb} and keep walking.

At night, Waffles sleeps on a soft {noun} next to my bed. If he cannot fall asleep, sing him a song about {plural noun}. That always works.

Waffles is a little bit afraid of the vacuum and the {noun}. If he hides under the table, just give him a hug.

We will be home on Sunday. Waffles will be so happy that he will probably be {verb ending in ing} by the front door.

Thanks again,
The Garcia Family

title: Have You Seen Mr. Whiskers?
text:
LOST CAT

Have you seen our cat, Mr. Whiskers? We could not find him on Tuesday afternoon at our house on Elm Street.

Mr. Whiskers is orange and white with a {adjective} tail. He wears a little blue collar with a bell shaped like a {noun}. He loves to nap in sunny spots and eat {plural noun}.

If you see him, please do not chase him. Just call his name {adverb} and shake a bag of treats. He will {verb} right over to you.

UPDATE: WE FOUND HIM!

Mr. Whiskers was never really lost. He was inside our house the whole time, curled up in a basket of {plural noun} in the laundry room. My dad found him when he heard something {verb ending in ing} under the socks.

Thank you to all our neighbors who helped look. To say thank you, we are having a party with lemonade and {food} on Saturday. Mr. Whiskers {past tense verb} when he heard the news.

title: Maple Street Pet Show Results
text:
Here are the official results of the Maple Street Pet Show. Thank you to every pet who came, and to the judges, who were very {adjective}.

Best Trick: Cooper the beagle. Cooper can sit, roll over, and {verb} when you ask him. He also brought the judges a {noun} as a gift.

Fluffiest Pet: Snowball the bunny. Snowball is so fluffy that one judge thought she was a pile of {plural noun}.

Best Costume: Bubbles the goldfish, who came dressed as a {noun}. Bubbles stayed in her bowl and swam {adverb} for the crowd.

Loudest Pet: Captain the parrot. Captain said "{silly word}" over and over for {number} minutes.

Best Friend: Every single pet. Each one went home with a ribbon and a bag of {plural noun}.

All of the owners {past tense verb} with joy. We will see you next year!

title: Diary of a Goldfish
text:
Monday: Today I swam around my bowl. Then I swam around it again. It was very {adjective}.

Tuesday: The big human named Leo tapped on my glass and said hello. I said hello back, but it came out as bubbles. Leo fed me some fish flakes and a tiny {noun}. Yum!

Wednesday: Leo put a new castle in my bowl. It has a door, two windows, and a picture of {plural noun} on the side. I will {verb} inside it every afternoon.

Thursday: The cat came to visit. She sat by my bowl and looked at me {adverb} for a long time. I made a funny face at her, and she {past tense verb} away.

Friday: Leo's grandma visited. She said I looked like a little {food}. I think that is a compliment.

Saturday: Leo cleaned my bowl. I spent the whole day {verb ending in ing} and blowing bubbles. Being a fish is the best job in the world, except maybe being a {noun}.

title: Welcome Home, Puppy
text:
Dear Puppy,

Welcome to our family! We are so happy you are here. My name is Ella, and I am going to be your best friend.

Here are some things you should know about your new home. Your bed is in the kitchen, next to the {noun}. Your water bowl is blue, and your food bowl is {color}. You may chew on your toys, but please do not chew on Dad's {plural noun}.

We have a big back yard. You can run and {verb} out there all day long. There is a tree, a swing, and a garden full of {plural noun}.

At night, I will read you a story about a {adjective} dog who saves the day. I will read it {adverb} so you can fall asleep.

I already picked a name for you. Your name is {silly word}. I hope you like it as much as I do.

Love,
Ella

P.S. When I came home from school today, you {past tense verb} so hard that your whole body wiggled.

title: Biscuit's Checkup Report
text:
Patient: Biscuit
Type of Animal: Dog
Age: Four years old

Today Biscuit came in for his yearly checkup. He walked in wagging his tail and wearing a {adjective} sweater. He is a very good boy.

We checked his ears, his eyes, and his teeth. His teeth are bright and shiny, like a row of {plural noun}. We listened to his heart, and it sounded just like a {noun}.

Biscuit is healthy and happy. His owner says he likes to {verb} in the back yard and nap on the couch.

Doctor's notes: Biscuit should keep going for walks every day. He may have one dog treat after dinner, plus a small bowl of {plural noun} on special days. Please brush his fur {adverb} once a week.

At the end of the visit, Biscuit {past tense verb} and gave the doctor a big lick on the {body part}. We gave him a sticker that says "I Was {adjective} Today!" See you next year, Biscuit!

title: My Weekend with Shelly the Turtle
text:
This weekend it was my turn to take home Shelly, our class turtle. Here is my report for Mr. Reed.

On Friday, Dad carried Shelly's tank to the car. Shelly rode in the back seat next to a bag of {plural noun}. She looked very {adjective} the whole ride.

On Saturday, I gave Shelly some lettuce and a little piece of {food}. She ate it {adverb}. Then I put her in a shallow box on the grass so she could {verb} in the sunshine. My little brother read her a book about {plural noun}.

On Sunday, we had a turtle race. Shelly raced against my brother's toy {noun}. It took her {number} minutes to cross the finish line, but she won!

Shelly was a great guest. When I put her back in her tank, she {past tense verb} at me. I think that means she wants to come back soon.

title: Meet Clover, Bunny of the Week
text:
Meet Clover, our Bunny of the Week at the Happy Paws Animal Shelter!

Clover is a soft brown bunny with big floppy ears and a {adjective} nose. She is two years old and very friendly.

Things Clover loves: carrots, cuddles, and {plural noun}. She also loves to {verb} in the morning while the other bunnies are still sleeping.

Things Clover does not love: loud noises and {plural noun}. If she hears something surprising, she hops {adverb} to her favorite hiding spot, which is under a {noun}.

Fun fact: Clover can jump as high as a {noun}. Our helpers clapped the first time they saw it.

Clover is looking for a family who will give her lots of love and a cozy place to sleep. If you think Clover would be a {adjective} friend, come visit us this Saturday. She will be {verb ending in ing} by the door, waiting to meet you!

title: How to Teach a Dog to Sit
text:
Teaching a dog to sit is easy if you follow these steps. I taught my dog, Noodle, and now he is the best sitter on our street.

Step one: Find a quiet place with no {plural noun} around. Dogs get distracted very easily.

Step two: Hold a treat above your dog's nose. Noodle likes treats that smell like {food}.

Step three: Move the treat back over his head {adverb}. He will look up, and his back legs will fold down all by themselves.

Step four: When he sits, say "Good dog!" in a {adjective} voice and give him the treat. You can also {verb} to show him how proud you are.

Step five: Practice every day for {number} days. Some dogs learn fast, and some dogs need more time.

If your dog does not sit, do not worry. The first time I tried, Noodle {past tense verb} and ran off to chase a {noun}. Now he sits, shakes hands, and even rolls over.

Next, I am going to teach him to {verb} while {verb ending in ing}. Wish us luck!

title: You Are Invited to Pepper's Party
text:
You are invited to a birthday party for Pepper the hamster! Pepper is turning one, and she wants to celebrate with all her friends.

When: Saturday at two o'clock
Where: The Lopez house, in the living room next to the {noun}

What to bring: A small gift for Pepper. She loves sunflower seeds, tiny {plural noun}, and anything {color}.

At the party, we will play Pin the Tail on the {animal}. We will also watch Pepper run on her wheel. She runs very {adverb}, so do not blink!

We will eat a big cake shaped like a {noun}. Pepper will get her own tiny cake made of carrots and {plural noun}.

Please do not {verb} near Pepper's cage. She gets {adjective} when there is too much noise.

Pepper cannot wait to see you. When we practiced singing "Happy Birthday" yesterday, she {past tense verb} with joy.

Love,
Pepper and Mia
